title: Hilton Jefferson and the 'hi-de-ho' answers
summary: Thomas laid out under Cab's singing and recalls coaxing stage-frightened Jeff to sing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: See, I had this premonition to not have all them other notes we was playin' while Cab was singing. We just laid out because we had to do the "hi-de-ho", we had to answer the "hi-de-ho." And that made sense that the rhythm section played...
This tempo, yeah. And "hi-de-hi-de..." I used to have the hardest time getting Jeff to sing. Because Jeff didn't like to sing. He didn't think he could carry a tune.
Hilton Jefferson you're talking about. A great, great alto saxophone player.
Yeah. He played beautiful. I told Jeff, "All Negroes..." We used the word "Negro" then. "All Negroes can sing." And he was there, but he just didn't think he could sing. I used to kid him about that.
So that's what made it. Now, we didn't have no idea that this song was going to be big. This was something that Mills had, and he was promoting it because it was a public domain song...
